guidelines.detail: refines EVT-01 (The reference models the process start as a plain start event followed by a task for the company's identification of the need, while the generated model uses a start event labeled with that action (X1), and the reference start event has no counterpart (M6). The description (S1) states the beginning as an action performed by the company, which is performed work and so fits a task. EVT-01 already sa)

refines FID-02 (The generated model turned the described opening action (identifying the need) into the start event label and left no task for it, so the reference task has no counterpart (M1), and the generated start event has no reference counterpart (X1). The description states the action as performed work by the company (S1), and the reference start event (M6) shows that the trigger and the action are separat)

new guideline (M1 shows the optional 'conduct interview' activity from the description ('may also conduct site visits or interviews') was dropped, and the generated model has no decision branch for it. No documented guideline covers optional-activity branching. LRN-005 covers alternative means of the same step and LRN-003 covers conditional clauses after an activity's outcome, so neither says this directly; this)
kept for this example only, tied to it by: both

same as LRN-005 (The reference splits the optional step into two named forms on an exclusive gateway, and the generated model has only one form. The reference also merges through its own gateway before the next step, while the generated model sends the bypass and the optional form straight to a shared merge. This is the omission that LRN-005 targets, placed inside an optional branch, so the guideline is essentiall)

same as LRN-005 (The records show the reference models the 'or' alternatives as a gateway with separate tasks, and the generated model merged them into one task labeled with the full alternative list (P3, M1), so the gateway that gives the choice is also missing (M2). The same mismatch is already covered by LRN-005, so this proposal duplicates it rather than adding a new rule.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when an actor performs an action of its own, such as identifying a need, rather than when an external message or condition arrives: Model a plain start event for the stated beginning of the process, with a label that names only the trigger state and not the actor's action. Model the actor's action as a task placed after the start event and connected to it by a sequence flow, and keep that task before the next described step. Do not use the action as the start event's label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process begins when an actor performs an action of its own, such as identifying a need, rather than when an external message or condition arrives

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description's opening sentence states an action that a participant performs to start the process (for example, recognising or identifying a situation), and the process then continues with further described work: Model the stated opening action as a task placed after the start event, so that the start event represents the trigger and the task represents the performed work. Do not use the start event label alone to stand for that action, and do not drop the action from the model.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description's opening sentence states an action that a participant performs to start the process (for example, recognising or identifying a situation), and the process then continues with further described work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an activity may also be performed as an optional extra step, on top of the main path, so it is not performed in every case (signalled by wording such as 'may also'): Place an exclusive gateway on the path at the point where the optional activity could occur. Give the optional activity its own outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, and give a bypass flow that skips it. Merge the optional branch and the bypass with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Keep the required activities on the main path unconditional and do not drop the optional activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an activity may also be performed as an optional extra step, on top of the main path, so it is not performed in every case (signalled by wording such as 'may also')

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a closing outcome as two passive clauses joined by 'and' in one sentence (for example, one thing is completed and another thing is carried out), with no single actor named for both clauses: Model each clause as its own task, labeled with the action the clause names, in the order the description gives, connected by a sequence flow. If the description states the first clause as a prerequisite of the second, place the prerequisite task before the second task. Do not merge the clauses into one task with a joined label, even when one clause reads as a summary of the other.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a closing outcome as two passive clauses joined by 'and' in one sentence (for example, one thing is completed and another thing is carried out), with no single actor named for both clauses

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names two or more alternative ways to carry out the same step, joined by 'or' (for example, the step may be done by one of several named means), and the model would otherwise keep only one of them: Place an exclusive gateway before the alternatives. Give each named alternative its own task on a separate outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, using the action the description names for it. Merge the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Do not drop any named alternative and do not leave the choice as one unconditional flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an optional activity may be carried out in one of several named forms joined by 'or', so it is not always performed, and the generated model keeps only one of the named forms or drops the choice
